case_title: Harpal Singh @ Chhota v. State of Punjab
accused_occupation: Municipal Councillor (appellant Sukhmeet Singh); occupation of other appellant not stated
accused_victim_relationship: Acquaintance (appellant Sukhmeet Singh, a Municipal Councillor known to the victim without personal intimacy); appellant Harpal Singh unknown to the victim before the incident; otherwise Stranger
statutory_provisions: IPC s.364A, s.395, s.412, s.471, s.120B; Arms Act s.25 (Harpal Singh only)
weapon: Revolver (.32 bore, victim's licensed revolver) and country-made pistol with live cartridge; victim's cash, cell phone and car keys taken at gunpoint
evidence_type: Eyewitness (victim); father's testimony on ransom calls; recovery evidence on disclosure statements; lender testimony identifying marked currency notes; call details (held inadmissible); finger print expert evidence
confession: Disclosure statements by accused leading to recoveries, relied on as admissible under s.27 Evidence Act; no confession to police described
aggravating_circumstances: Victim held captive about two days, chained, blindfolded and drugged; repeated threats to kill victim and family; ransom demand of Rs. 5 crores later pursued
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under the charged sections (IPC ss.364A, 395, 412, 471, 120B; Arms Act s.25 for Harpal Singh); sentences ranging from one year to life imprisonment with fine, running concurrently
high_court_outcome: Appeals dismissed; conviction and sentence upheld
offence_finally_established: Conspiracy and abduction for ransom under IPC s.364A, s.395, s.412, s.471 and s.120B; Arms Act s.25 for Harpal Singh
neutral_facts: The victim, who was involved in real estate, was contacted by phone by a caller offering a land deal, and over several weeks the callers built his confidence in the proposal. On the morning of the planned meeting, the victim went to the site in his own car. Several men arrived in a Honda City car; one pointed a revolver at him, his cell phone, car keys and cash were taken, his face was covered, his mouth was taped and his hands were tied, and he was forced into the dicky of the Honda City car. For about two days he was held captive and moved between places. He was chained, blindfolded and given drugs, and he heard his captors address each other by nicknames. The captors repeatedly phoned his father demanding ransom, first Rs. 5 crores and later Rs. 1 crore, threatening that the victim and family would be killed if it was not paid. The father raised money from several lenders, some of whom had marked packets of notes with initials. Money was thrown from a moving train as instructed, and the victim was released. Police registered an FIR, arrested the accused and, on their disclosure statements, recovered cash, firearms, the Honda City car, and the victim's driving licence and tape from the car's dicky. Telephone call records were collected, but no certificate was obtained for them. No identification parade was held. The victim identified the accused in later testimony.
physical_harm: No specific injuries recorded; victim's hands and feet chained, mouth taped, blindfolded and drugged during captivity; no death
number_of_offences: 13 charged (11 IPC sections plus Arms Act ss.25 and 27 per charge-sheet); 5 IPC sections finally upheld for both appellants (s.364A, s.395, s.412, s.471, s.120B), plus Arms Act s.25 for Harpal Singh
financial_property_loss: Ransom of about Rs. 1 crore paid in two bags thrown from a train; Rs. 15,000 cash, licensed revolver and cell phone taken from victim
premeditation_planning: Yes: court found a conspiratorial build-up through the land-deal lure and deliberate timing of the abduction
key_evidence_accepted: Victim's testimony (identification and captivity account); father PW2's account of ransom calls; disclosure-based recoveries of cash, firearms, Honda City car and victim's driving licence; lender testimony and PW14's identification of marked notes
witness_credibility: Victim's evidence found truthful and substantially unshaken by cross-examination; father's evidence of ransom calls detailed; lenders' testimony not lightly ignored
post_offence_conduct: Disclosure statements led police to recovery sites (cash, firearms, Honda City car); no absconding by appellants noted
trial_duration: offence: 09.01.2008; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 21.04.2014; Supreme Court: 21.11.2016
legal_representation: For appellants: R. Basant and Subromaniam Prasad (senior advocates); for State: V. Madhukar, AAG
investigation_status: FIR registered 11.01.2008; charge-sheet laid; 27 prosecution witnesses examined; trial completed; no TIP held
procedural_irregularity: No s.65B(4) certificate for call details, which were held inadmissible; no test identification parade held; no independent witness present at Harpal Singh's disclosure statement
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted and sentenced; High Court: appeals dismissed, conviction and sentence sustained; Supreme Court: appeals dismissed
prosecution_argument: Evidence taken as a whole proves the abduction-for-ransom conspiracy beyond reasonable doubt; recoveries and cash linkage support guilt; no interference warranted
defence_argument: Harpal Singh's complicity unproved; call details inadmissible without s.65B certificate; no TIP; victim did not name him in earlier statements; recoveries unconnected; Sukhmeet Singh alleged political vendetta and that cash belonged to his father's land sale
legal_principle_applied: Conspiracy elements (agreement as act, intention as mens rea; unity of object suffices); s.27 Evidence Act recoveries admissible; s.65B(4) certificate mandatory for electronic records; omission to name accused at first instance not fatal
precedent_relied_upon: Relied on: Anvar P.V. v. P.K. Basheer (2014) 10 SCC 473; Pullukuri Kotayya v. King Emperor AIR 1947 PC 67; Bodhraj @ Bodha v. State of J&K (2002) 8 SCC 45. Referred to: Ferozuddin Basheeruddin v. State of Kerala (2001) 7 SCC 596; Mir Nagvi Askari v. CBI (2009) 15 SCC 643; Mohd. Amin v. CBI (2008) 15 SCC 49
other_sentence_order: Registry directed to transmit original record to the Trial Court
